A1.justification: Both complete 41-page PDFs describe Meta-rater and contain matching main sections and Appendices A–I. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures without material gaps.

before.justification: v3 reports original pre-training experiments, quality-rater evaluations, and ablations. For example, Table 1 reports average accuracy of 47.01 for Meta-rater versus 43.78 for random selection.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the pre-training comparisons in Table 1, rating-model evaluations, scaling experiments, and detailed appendix results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, proxy-model training, LightGBM loss prediction, weight selection and averaging, and PRRC rating procedures are unchanged. No method component or architecture is revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SlimPajama training coverage, eight primary downstream benchmarks, MMLU and NaturalQuestions evaluations, and Common Crawl-only scenario. No dataset, task, or domain coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including Random, PPL, Semdedup, DSIR, QuRating, Fineweb-Edu, MATES, individual PRRC raters, and Mean/Intersection combinations.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, domain proportions, annotation splits, evaluation metrics, and few-shot settings remain unchanged. The altered plotting axes in Figures 2–3 do not change the evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The same analyses of quality-score weights and correlations, proxy-model count and size, combination strategies, domain diversity, and rating examples are retained. Figures 2–3 redisplay existing analyses without adding tests.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version supplies evaluation uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run and seed details that are absent from the other.

E6.justification: All result tables are unchanged. Figures 2–3 only round existing labels to one decimal, such as 56.29 to 56.3 and 31.35 to 31.4; detailed results remain in Tables 17–18. No result entries or findings change.

T1.justification: The task formulation, aggregation and regression mathematics, and FLOP approximations in Equations 1–4 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same PRRC and Meta-rater contributions, doubled-convergence claim, reported 3.23-point downstream gain, and scaling claims through 7.2B parameters.

C2.justification: Interpretations of metric complementarity, diminishing returns from additional proxy models, and domain diversity are unchanged. The limitations concerning model scale, token budgets, and incomplete quality-metric coverage are also retained.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 removes the two direct Hugging Face links for ModernBERT-base and ModernBERT-large, formerly footnotes 11–12. Model names, technical settings, hardware information, and the project release link remain; this reduces access documentation without establishing any change in resource availability.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, bibliography, and research positioning are unchanged. The ModernBERT paper citation remains despite removal of the two model-access footnotes.

P1.justification: Local text edits include spelling out task names in the redrawn plots, removing two URL footnotes, and updating the arXiv version/date stamp. The prose and section and appendix organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 2–3 are redrawn with horizontal rounded labels, full task names, smaller typography, different colors, and y-axis ticks spanning 20–65 instead of 30–60. Resizing these plots and removing footnotes produces limited text reflow; other figures and table displays are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The redraws reduce label crowding and spell out task names, but use smaller text; two direct model links are removed while model identities and the project link remain. With the scientific content and complete appendix evidence unchanged, these limited presentation and access edits leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
